title: Accessibility: colour blindness, contrast and never relying on colour alone

videos.script: Here are two lines on a chart, one red and one green. South and Northeast. They cross in 2024, and that crossing is the story. {{chart}} Now here is the same chart as about one man in twelve sees it. {{simulated}} Both lines are the same muddy olive. The crossing is still there. Nobody can tell which line went up. {{olive}} This is not a rare problem, and it is not only about colour blindness. A pale grey line on a white page, a chart printed in black and white, a projector in a bright room, a phone in the sun. Each one takes something away from the reader. {{rare}} Accessibility is designing so that a chart survives all of that. It has measurable rules: how much contrast text needs, how much a line needs, and one simple rule above the rest. Never let colour carry a meaning on its own. {{rules}} In this lesson you will simulate colour blindness, measure contrast, and redraw the chart so it reads for everyone. {{plan}}
